translation.title: Terbinafine Hydrochloride Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for skin fungal infections caused by dermatophytes (tinea pedis (athlete's foot), tinea cruris (jock itch), tinea corporis (ringworm of the body)), and for tinea versicolor caused by Pityrosporum orbiculare and cutaneous candidiasis.
translation.usage: Apply it to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day. Treatment duration by condition: tinea pedis (athlete's foot) - once a day for 1 week; interdigital (between-the-toes) tinea pedis - twice a day for 1 week; plantar (sole) tinea pedis - twice a day for 2 weeks; tinea corporis and tinea cruris (jock itch) - 1 to 2 weeks; cutaneous candidiasis - 1 to 2 weeks; tinea versicolor - 2 weeks.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you are breastfeeding, or for children. Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping unless directed by a doctor. For candidiasis, do not use acidic soap. For external use only. Do not use it in the eyes (not for ophthalmic use, not on the cornea or conjunctiva); if it accidentally gets into the eyes it may irritate them and, rarely, a latent fungal infection may worsen, so rinse thoroughly with plenty of water. Do not use it on the nails, scalp, around the mouth, or on the vaginal area. If symptoms do not improve after the treatment period, consult a doctor or pharmacist. Adverse reactions may occur - hypersensitivity with rash, excessive irritation, hives, redness, rash, erythema (red patches), itching, irritation, local contact dermatitis, skin peeling, crusting of wounds, pigmentation abnormalities, stinging and a burning sensation; if any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature and keep out of reach of children.
